behavioral_notes.observation: Visitor-to-operator matching is a multi-criteria load balancer, not visible in metadata. _compute_available_operator_ids first filters res.users by live presence (presence_ids.status=='online'), max_sessions limit, and block_assignment_during_call (skip agents in a call). _get_operator then runs a raw SQL query over im_livechat.channel.member.history + discuss_channel_rtc_session to rank agents by active-chat count and in-call status, applies a preference ladder (same_language -> all/one expertise -> same_country -> least-active), honours a 120s BUFFER_TIME between two sessions for the same operator, sticks to previous_operator_id when still suitable, and otherwise picks the least-active via random tie-break.

Channel routing: a live chat session is materialized as a discuss.channel with channel_type='livechat'. The vals builder assembles channel_member_ids (one 'agent'/'bot' member for the operator plus a 'visitor' member for the mail.guest or logged-in res.users), sets livechat_operator_id, livechat_channel_id, livechat_status='in_progress', livechat_failure ('no_answer' for human agent else 'no_failure'), and—when the operator_model is 'chatbot.script'—seeds chatbot_current_step_id from the script's welcome steps. A CHECK constraint enforces livechat_operator_id is non-null for livechat channels. The controller (/im_livechat/get_session) then _broadcast()s the channel to the operator over the bus.

discuss.channel inherits rating.mixin with _rating_get_parent_field_name()='livechat_channel_id' so each session's rating rolls up to its im_livechat.channel (rating.parent.mixin, _rating_satisfaction_days=14). The /im_livechat/feedback controller creates exactly ONE rating.rating per session (1/3/5 = bad/ok/good), posts a o_mail_notification feedback message, and sets rated_partner_id to the operator. Escalation is derived: livechat_is_escalated = (len(agent history) > 1) and livechat_outcome computes to 'escalated' / 'no_answer' / 'no_agent' / 'no_failure'; _forward_human_operator hands a chatbot/AI conversation off to a live agent (adds the agent member, removes the bot, rebroadcasts).

behavioral_notes.element: session lifecycle, bus push & autovacuum GC
behavioral_notes.observation: Closing is event-driven, not state-machine metadata: _close_livechat_session / _action_unfollow set livechat_end_dt when the visitor or the last operator leaves, leave any RTC call, post a 'Visitor left' notification, and bus_send the update. write() pushes 'need_help' (looking-for-help) deltas to the im_livechat_group_user bus subchannel so any operator can claim the chat (livechat_join_channel_needing_help). Two @api.autovacuum crons garbage-collect empty livechat sessions older than 1h and bot-only idle sessions older than 1 day.

behavioral_notes.element: embeddable livechat OWL widget (Shadow DOM) + CORS routing
behavioral_notes.observation: The visitor-facing UI is an OWL app, LivechatRoot, rendering ChatHub + LivechatButton inside a Shadow DOM (styles isolated from the host site). External sites embed it via a <script> tag pointing at /im_livechat/loader/<channel_id>, which boots from the im_livechat.assets_embed_external bundle; the LivechatController._is_cors_request() detects cross-origin requests (referer host/scheme mismatch) and swaps to im_livechat.assets_embed_cors so all RPCs route to the /im_livechat/cors/* public endpoints with cors='*'. The im_livechat.livechat OWL service holds session state and persists the previous operator in expirableStorage.

value_streams: Visitor-to-Resolution: website visitor opens chat -> rule/chatbot match -> operator assignment (or bot) -> live conversation over bus -> optional escalation/hand-off -> session close -> rating + transcript
policies: 3 record rules + 15 ACLs scoping operator vs manager vs public/guest access to channels and sessions

BUFFER_TIME (120s) anti-flood between two sessions for the same operator; max_sessions / block_assignment_during_call capacity caps
autovacuum GC of empty (1h) and bot-only idle (1d) sessions

im_livechat.channel rating satisfaction (last 14 days), ongoing_session_count, remaining_session_capacity

classification.rationale: im_livechat is a value-network (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating technology): its core value is connecting website visitors with operators/chatbots in real time over the bus, and the central asset is the matching/routing layer (_get_operator: availability, language, expertise, country, load balancing) that mediates between two populations of customers (visitors and agents). It runs the network-infrastructure-operation activity (provisioning + operating the chat service) and the network-promotion/contract-management activity (channel rules, auto-popup, chatbot gating). It is the primary customer-service provisioning activity (APQC 6.0 Manage Customer Service), building on mail/discuss + bus rather than moving a document down a chain.

standard_capabilities: Embeddable live chat widget (Shadow-DOM OWL) for Odoo and external/CORS sites
Operator assignment by availability + language + expertise + country + least-active load balancing
Channel rules (per-URL regex, per-country, auto-popup timer, show/hide button)
Scripted chatbots with steps/answers, email validation, forward-to-operator hand-off
Per-session satisfaction rating, feedback message, review-link redirect
Conversation tags, internal notes, looking-for-help / escalation queue over the bus
Live chat analytics (im_livechat.report.channel) and digest KPIs
typical_fits: Website customer support / pre-sales chat out of the box
Embedding the widget on a non-Odoo marketing site via the loader + CORS endpoints
common_gaps: Custom routing/SLA logic beyond the built-in preference ladder and buffer
Advanced AI/LLM agents beyond scripted chatbot.script (separate module/integration)
Deep CRM/helpdesk hand-off (lead/ticket creation) requires bridge modules (crm_livechat, helpdesk)
Channel-specific working-hours / availability calendars beyond live presence
Custom satisfaction surveys beyond the 3-point good/ok/bad rating
